title: additionalProperties variants
description: A fixture, not a production schema. Six ways an object can declare additionalProperties, so the generator's handling of each is a test result rather than a claim. See PSD-0001 §6.

propsTrue.description: Known fields plus arbitrary extras — the combination people usually reach for. Generates an unusable field; see the test.

propsFalse.description: Closed object. What every schema under docs/jsonschema/character/v1alpha uses.

propsTyped.description: Known fields plus extras constrained to one type.

bareTrue.description: Free-form object. The case the generator handles correctly.

bareTyped.description: Free-form object with a typed value. Also handled correctly.

propsOmitted.description: The control: additionalProperties absent, which JSON Schema treats as true.

propsEmptySchema.description: The spelling that looks like a workaround and is not: `{}` is the same schema as `true` in JSON Schema, and the generator treats it identically.

openViaMethods.description: Workaround 1. Structurally identical to propsTrue; the difference is entirely in Go, where workarounds.go supplies UnmarshalJSON and MarshalJSON on the generated type. No schema change is needed to make properties+true work.

openViaExtension.description: Workaround 2. The seam goes in the schema instead: goJSONSchema substitutes a map-shaped hand-written type. Note this is a $defs entry, so the generator emits `type OpenViaExtension OpenBag` — a defined type, which does NOT inherit methods. A map shape survives that; a struct with custom marshalling would not.

typedViaMarshal.description: Workaround 3. Structurally identical to propsTyped. Here the generator DOES emit UnmarshalJSON and decoding is already correct, so workarounds.go supplies MarshalJSON alone — which is never generated, so there is no collision.
